html:
The Rumsen were the Ohlone people of the Monterey Peninsula and the lower Carmel River in central California. They spoke Rumsen, one of the Ohlone (Costanoan) languages, and lived by fishing, gathering shellfish and acorns, and hunting.

In 1770 Spain founded the presidio of Monterey, the capital of Alta California, in their country, and Junípero Serra moved his mission to the Carmel River as Mission San Carlos Borromeo. The Rumsen were drawn into the mission alongside the Esselen to the south, and disease and forced labour cut their numbers sharply. Some of the first records of an Ohlone language were made among them. Their descendants are part of today's Ohlone and Esselen communities.
